  <h2 id="how" class="course-page-section">How a project is organized</h2>
  <div class="qft-exams-how">
    <div class="course-page-card"><h3>Goals</h3><ul><li>Applying the knowledge gained to real scientific problems.</li><li>Mastering the tools of research: LaTeX, git, python.</li><li>Developing the skills of working together on projects.</li><li>Critical thinking and creativity: the projects encourage unconventional solutions and well-argued conclusions.</li></ul></div>
    <div class="course-page-card"><h3>Structure of the report</h3><ol><li>Introduction: motivation, a short review of the literature, statement of the problem.</li><li>Theory: derivations, calculations, formulas.</li><li>Practical part: simulation, data analysis, calculations.</li><li>Discussion: plots, tables, interpretation of the results.</li><li>Conclusions: the main results and how the work could be continued.</li><li>References: all sources used.</li></ol></div>
    <div class="course-page-card"><h3>Technical aspects</h3><ul><li>Write the project in LaTeX; the online service overleaf.com is convenient.</li><li>Feynman diagrams: the tikz-feynman package.</li><li>Plots: the matplotlib library.</li></ul></div>
  </div>
  <p class="course-page-note">The projects are updated and expanded, so check back regularly.</p>
